column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Discrete seawater samples were collected from surface, mid-depth, and bottom water layers with a Niskin water sampler: 1.7 l for Washington State; 2.2 l for Hawaii 2001-02; Kemmerer bottle water sampler used by EMAP-West States of California and Oregon
column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: An otter trawling is a large net dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.
column66: The recommended 10-d sediment toxicity test with H. azteca must be conducted at 23 deg C with a 16L:8D photoperiod at an illuminance of about 100 to 1000 lux . Test chambers are 300-mL high-form lipless beakers containing 100 mL of sediment and 175 mL of overlying water.

This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: An otter trawling is a large net dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net.

column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation. column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.
column66: The recommended 10-d sediment toxicity test with H. azteca must be conducted at 23 deg C with a 16L:8D photoperiod at an illuminance of about 100 to 1000 lux . Test chambers are 300-mL high-form lipless beakers containing 100 mL of sediment and 175 mL of overlying water.

column59: Discrete seawater samples were collected from surface, mid-depth, and bottom water layers with a Niskin water sampler: 1.7 l for Washington State; 2.2 l for Hawaii 2001-02; Kemmerer bottle water sampler used by EMAP-West States of California and Oregon
column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.
column71: Filtered water and filters were frozen until analysis.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: An otter trawling is a large net dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Discrete seawater samples were collected from surface, mid-depth, and bottom water layers with a Niskin water sampler: 1.7 l for Washington State; 2.2 l for Hawaii 2001-02; Kemmerer bottle water sampler used by EMAP-West States of California and Oregon
column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: In otter trawling a large net, is dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net. The net is dragged behind the boat with a thick steel cable.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column2: EPA National Aquatic Resources Survey (NARS)
column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.
column66: The recommended 10-d sediment toxicity test with H. azteca must be conducted at 23 deg C with a 16L:8D photoperiod at an illuminance of about 100 to 1000 lux . Test chambers are 300-mL high-form lipless beakers containing 100 mL of sediment and 175 mL of overlying water.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: An otter trawling is a large net dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: An otter trawling is a large net dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.

In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. column59: Discrete seawater samples were collected from surface, mid-depth, and bottom water layers with a Niskin water sampler: 1.7 l for Washington State; 2.2 l for Hawaii 2001-02; Kemmerer bottle water sampler used by EMAP-West States of California and Oregon
column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.
column71: Filtered water and filters were frozen until analysis.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: An otter trawling is a large net dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: An otter trawling is a large net dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net.

column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. column59: Discrete seawater samples were collected from surface, mid-depth, and bottom water layers with a Niskin water sampler: 1.7 l for Washington State; 2.2 l for Hawaii 2001-02; Kemmerer bottle water sampler used by EMAP-West States of California and Oregon
column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.
column66: The recommended 10-d sediment toxicity test with H. azteca must be conducted at 23 deg C with a 16L:8D photoperiod at an illuminance of about 100 to 1000 lux . Test chambers are 300-mL high-form lipless beakers containing 100 mL of sediment and 175 mL of overlying water.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. column59: Discrete seawater samples were collected from surface, mid-depth, and bottom water layers with a Niskin water sampler: 1.7 l for Washington State; 2.2 l for Hawaii 2001-02; Kemmerer bottle water sampler used by EMAP-West States of California and Oregon
column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: An otter trawling is a large net dragged along the bottom or up in the water column behind a towing vessel. The mouth of the net is held open by two large "doors" which are attached to either side of the net.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Discrete seawater samples were collected from surface, mid-depth, and bottom water layers with a Niskin water sampler: 1.7 l for Washington State; 2.2 l for Hawaii 2001-02; Kemmerer bottle water sampler used by EMAP-West States of California and Oregon
column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.

column59: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.

column59: Discrete seawater samples were collected from surface, mid-depth, and bottom water layers with a Niskin water sampler: 1.7 l for Washington State; 2.2 l for Hawaii 2001-02; Kemmerer bottle water sampler used by EMAP-West States of California and Oregon
column66: Duplicate water samples from the same cast were filtered aboard ship with 0.7-micron glass-fiber filter pads (not all duplicates were analyzed).  Nutrients and chlorophyll a: a disposable, graduated 50-cc polypropylene syringe fitted with a stainless steel or polypropylene filtering assembly was used to filter a parent water sample through 25 or 47 mm GF/F filters.  100-1,500 ml seawater was filtered. 1 ml of saturated MgCO3 was then filtered through each pad to buffer the chlorophyll sample against degradation.  Approximately 40 ml of filtrate was preserved for nutrient analyses in a 60 ml HPDE or Nalgene bottle.  Total suspended solids: approximately 1 liter of unfiltered seawater was taken from the water sampler at discrete depths and poured into a 1 L polypropylene bottle. Both the filtered water and filters were immediately frozen.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.

column57: NCA Standard Sediment Sample for multiple analysis
column59: Sediments are collected for a variety of analyses. One sample is collected for benthic species composition and abundance, and additional sediment grabs are collected for chemical analyses (organics/metals and TOC), grain size determination, and for use in acute whole sediment toxicity tests. The number of grabs needed may vary based on the sediment characteristics. While the biology grab is being processed (sieved), grabs should be collected for chemistry, grain size and toxicity tests. These grabs will be composited, mixed and split into four separate sample containers. A minimum of 4L of sediment will be required for the chemistry and toxicity samples.
column61: A 1/25 (0.04) m2, stainless steel, Young-modified Van Veen Grab (or similar) sampler is appropriate for collecting sediment samples for both biological and chemical analyses. The top of the sampler is either hinged or otherwise removable so the top layer of sediment can be easily removed for chemical and toxicity sample collection. This gear is relatively easy to operate and requires little specialized training.
